successors.note: The state was a federal state of the German Empire from 1871 and ended in November 1918 (see the dissolve event); the Weimar Republic took over its land (Republic of Baden (Free People's Republic of Baden)). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-53 D01, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire; same change as fx-46 R122 for Bavaria); the hierarchy.csv row grand-duchy-of-baden -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.

region.text: the Electorate of Baden enlarged by Pressburg and the mediatisations, as the grand duchy of 1806

ledger.note: 1806: Baden becomes a grand duchy. Infobox: 'Established: Electorate on 27 April 1803; Grand Duchy on 24 October 1806' (the event carries no month so that it sorts before the year's mediatisation gain, which no page dates); 'In 1806, Charles Frederick joined the Confederation of the Rhine, declared himself a sovereign prince and grand duke' (the Confederation page gives 12 July 1806 for the accession; the mediatisation page says the Confederation was founded on 12 June). The page names the lands won, not a boundary.

region.text: the lands of Fürstenberg, Leiningen, Salm-Krautheim, Klettgau and the Knights of St John added to the Electorate by 1806

ledger.note: 1806: the second wave of mediatisation enlarges Baden. The Grand Duchy page: Baden gained 'ecclesiastical and secular territories' in the German mediatisation; the mediatisation page's table lists under Baden the Prince of Fürstenberg, the Prince of Leiningen, 'Prince of Salm-Reifferscheid-Krautheim: right bank', 'Prince of Schwarzenberg: Klettgau' and the Knights of St John's 'bailiwick on upper Rhine' (the table is undated). The region is the growth between Cliopatria's Electorate of 1805 and Grand Duchy of 1806, which also holds the Breisgau of Pressburg (the Electorate dossier's December 1805 gain).

region.text: the accessions 'at the expense of the Kingdom of Württemberg'

ledger.note: 1809: Baden receives land from Württemberg. 'Baden was rewarded with accessions of territory at the expense of the Kingdom of Württemberg' (Grand Duchy page, dated there to the Treaty of Schönbrunn). The page names no places; the region is the growth between Cliopatria's 1806 and 1811 shapes, which extends the south edge from 47.60 to 47.53 N.

region.text: the grand duchy, held by the provisional government

ledger.note: 1849: the Grand Duke flees and Baden passes to the revolutionaries. 'That same night of 13/14 May Grand Duke Leopold flees from his residenz in Karlsruhe into exile at Koblenz'; a provisional democratic government under Lorenz Brentano is formed on 1 June. The page names no proclamation of a 'Republic of Baden'; Cliopatria draws one in 1849-1852.

region.text: the grand duchy, fought over by the provisional government and the invading Prussian and federal troops

ledger.note: 1849: Prussian and federal troops invade Baden in June. 'Two improvised Prussian army corps under the Prince of Prussia' join federal and Hessian troops in the invasion; the revolutionaries are beaten at Waghäusel on 21/22 June and a dictatorial government under Goegg and Werner forms on 28 June.

region.text: the grand duchy, occupied by Prussian troops

ledger.note: 1849: Prussian troops occupy Baden. 'The Prussians march into Freiburg unopposed' on 7 July 1849 (Baden Revolution page); the Grand Duchy page: 'Prussian troops occupied Baden for a time' after Leopold's return on 10 August.
1849: Rastatt falls and the revolution ends. 'After being surrounded for three weeks Rastatt surrenders to Groeben' on 23 July 1849; the Grand Duke returned on 10 August 1849 (Grand Duchy page).
1849: the grand duchy recovers its land from the rebels. The last fortress, Rastatt, surrenders on 23 July 1849; 'The Baden Army was disbanded and later rebuilt under Prussian leadership'.

1852: end of the Prussian occupation, bridged. The Grand Duchy page says only that 'Prussian troops occupied Baden for a time' and gives no end; 1852 is the last year of Cliopatria's Republic of Baden row and the year Leopold died and Frederick became regent.

region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: 14 November 1918: the Free People's Republic of Baden is formed. 'He renounced his governmental powers on 13 November, and abdicated on 22 November' (Frederick II); 'The Free People's Republic of Baden was formed on 14 November, and elections scheduled on 5 January 1919.' Infobox 'German Revolution: 14 November 1918', status 'German Empire (1871-1918)', succeeded by the 'Republic of Baden'. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: War of the Fifth Coalition

zones.text: the Württemberg land that Baden received

wars.outcome: Baden, a French ally, was 'rewarded with accessions of territory at the expense of the Kingdom of Württemberg' (Treaty of Schönbrunn, 1809).
wars.note: The Fifth Coalition article was not opened; the wording is the Grand Duchy page's.

wars.name: Baden Revolution
wars.outcome: The Grand Duke fled on 13/14 May 1849, Prussian and federal troops invaded in June, won at Waghäusel on 21/22 June and took Rastatt on 23 July 1849; Leopold returned on 10 August and Prussian troops occupied Baden 'for a time'.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Baden fielded a contingent for Austria, 'signed a treaty of peace and alliance with Prussia' on 17 August 1866 and withdrew from the German Confederation; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Baden's army fought on the German side; Baden joined the German Empire under the treaties of November 1870 and 1871.
wars.note: The war article was not opened.

certainty.note: Boundaries moved with the 1806 mediatisations and the 1809 Württemberg accessions, and the 1816 Munich treaty left Bavaria's claim to the Palatine parts of Baden open until 1819; no page gives a line.

After the 1819 Frankfurt treaty the pages record no boundary change; the 1849 revolution and the Prussian occupation moved authority, not borders. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes: CLIOPATRIA: no Grand Duchy of Baden shape for 1849-1852 (the rebellion; it draws a Republic of Baden of 17,733 km2 there, which belongs to republic-of-baden in another batch); a new keyframe 1849-1852 keeps the grand duchy, and the ledger carries the loss to the rebels (13/14 May), the Prussian-federal invasion (June), the Prussian occupation (7 July) and the recovery (23 July). The 1809 accession from Württemberg is drawn two years late (1811). The 1806 shape holds the Breisgau of Pressburg and the 1806 mediatisations together; the Electorate dossier (1803-1805) carries the December 1805 Breisgau gain and its 1805 shape is smaller, so the 1806 'gain' region overlaps that event; the mediatisation page's Baden list is undated. SILENCES: no page opened dates the end of the Prussian occupation (1852 is bridged), the 1815-1819 drop of 270 km2, or the 1870 growth of 178 km2; the Grand Duke's return on 10 August 1849 is in the Grand Duchy page, not the revolution page. DISAGREEMENTS: Confederation of the Rhine founded 12 July 1806 (Confederation page) or 12 June (mediatisation page); constitution 1814 or 1818; Frederick I's reign from 1856 or 1858. The 'Republic of Baden' is not named on the Baden Revolution page. Pages budget: 5 (Grand Duchy of Baden, Baden Revolution, Confederation of the Rhine, German Confederation, German mediatisation). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (grand-duchy-of-baden_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row grand-duchy-of-baden -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. The grand duke renounced his powers on 13 November and abdicated on 22 November 1918; the republic was formed on 14 November.
